classification_legend.LOGICALLY_EXPECTED: Every canonical mantra should have this. Target 100%; any shortfall is a gap.
classification_legend.TRADITION_EXPECTED: The tradition transmits this for the recension, so a shortfall is unfinished ingestion rather than a property of the text -- but it is not a logical necessity the way text or hierarchy is.
classification_legend.RECENSION_CONDITIONAL: Only applicable where the recension's witness carries the layer at all. State N/A per Veda, never zero.
classification_legend.OPTIONAL_ASSESSED: Not required per passage, but the assessed population is knowable because it is held outside the graph as an explicit catalog.
classification_legend.INHERENTLY_OPTIONAL: No mantra is required to have a positive value. What must reach 100% is HAVING BEEN ASSESSED, which is the number the graph cannot supply.

status_legend.OBSERVED_VALUE: A positive count measured from the live graph.
status_legend.VERIFIED_ZERO: Zero, and the graph or a measured registry record establishes the layer was examined and is genuinely absent.
status_legend.NOT_APPLICABLE: The recension's witness does not carry this layer.
status_legend.NOT_ASSESSED: Zero, and nothing records that the detection population ever included this Veda. NOT the same as VERIFIED_ZERO.

structural_defects.finding: The Atharvavedic SEARCH_DERIVATIVE layer deletes base letters instead of only accent marks. 5,134 of 5,839 AV mantras (87.94%) have a derivative missing at least one base letter present in the PRIMARY_TEXT: 11,582 lost 'm' (anusvara, written m + U+0323) and 5,139 lost 'r' (vocalic r, written r + U+0325). The normaliser decomposed each grapheme and dropped the base together with the combining-below mark, so 'kr̥dhi' is stored as 'kdhi' and 'parjanyaṃ' as 'parjanya'.
structural_defects.live_impact: search_service.py reads text_role='SEARCH_DERIVATIVE' at lines 269, 494 and 747, so the corruption is served. Probed live: /api/v1/search?q=kr̥dhi&veda=AV returns 0 passages although AVS 1.2.2 contains the word; q=namāśmānaṃ likewise returns 0.
structural_defects.measurement: Per-mantra NFD base-letter multiset diff of PRIMARY_TEXT against SEARCH_DERIVATIVE. Column search_derivative_intact in the CSV; -1 means the recension has no derivative layer.

structural_defects.finding: All 1,903 Yajurvedic translations carry source_id='SACRED_TEXTS', for which NO (:Source) node exists. Meanwhile (:Source {source_id:'GRIFFITH_WHITE_YAJURVEDA', name:'The Texts of the White Yajurveda, Griffith translation'}) exists and is referenced by nothing. The translation's own translator and work_edition fields name exactly that Griffith text, so the correct Source node is present and orphaned while the pointer dangles.
structural_defects.measurement: Set difference between source_id values on Translation/TextVersion and s.source_id on (:Source).

structural_defects.finding: (:Source) carries ZERO relationships of any type. Provenance is a bare string join from TextVersion.source_id / Translation.source_id to Source.source_id, with no edge and no constraint on the referencing side. Nothing prevents CORPUS_D02 from recurring, and provenance cannot be traversed in a graph query.

The 4,878 Atharvavedic translations are Whitney and Lanman (Harvard Oriental Series 7-8, 1905) by their own translator and work_edition fields, but carry source_id='VEDAWEB' -- a Source whose name in the graph is 'VedaWeb Rigveda public data'. (:Source {source_id:'WIKISOURCE_WHITNEY_AV', name:'Atharva-Veda Samhita, Whitney and Lanman translation'}) exists and is referenced by nothing. The source_id and the bibliographic fields disagree about who published the text.
structural_defects.measurement: Grouped Translation.source_id against Translation.translator and Translation.work_edition per Veda.

structural_defects.finding: Zero PADAPATHA TextVersion nodes exist, yet the RV (:Work) node's scope property -- which the API serves -- asserts 'Padapatha and the accented samhitapatha are carried as text versions of these same mantras', and data/registry/text_versions.yaml declares a VedaWeb layer with text_form PADAPATHA and text_role PADAPATHA. A committed claim in the graph contradicts the graph.
structural_defects.measurement: MATCH (t:TextVersion) WHERE t.text_form='PADAPATHA' OR t.text_role='PADAPATHA' RETURN count(t) => 0. Full text_form/text_role value space enumerated rather than grepped for the expected value.

structural_defects.finding: No Yajurvedic mantra has a PRIMARY_TEXT Sanskrit layer. All 1,975 carry exactly one canonical layer at text_role EXTRACTED_FROM_CONTAINER, whose own enum docstring states it 'must never be selected as primary_sanskrit: doing so would make an interpretive segmentation canonical'. Either the Yajurveda is being displayed from a role the model forbids as primary, or it has no primary text.

Parallel and reuse relationships are directed and asymmetric by Veda. No Yajurvedic mantra is ever the SUBJECT of a parallel edge: has_outgoing is 0 for all 1,975, while 687 have an incoming edge. REUSES_TEXT_FROM is emitted only from SV (1,662 subjects); the Rigveda's 1,421 are all incoming. AV has 1,332 outgoing and 0 incoming. A directed-outgoing coverage query therefore reports a false zero for the Yajurveda and a false zero for Rigvedic reuse.
structural_defects.measurement: Outgoing vs incoming counts per Veda over the five parallel types. The CSV columns are UNDIRECTED.

structural_defects.finding: The (:SourceArtifact) label is declared in db.labels() but holds ZERO nodes. Dimension 9's intended three-part provenance chain (Source / SourceArtifact / TextVersion) is missing its middle term entirely.

VG:YV:VSM:A20:V015 carries TextVersion.accented=true but its string holds no accent mark. Its only combining signs are U+1CEA and U+1CED, which are an anusvara sign and the Vedic tiryak sign, not tone marks. 1 of 1,975 Yajurvedic mantras.

structural_defects.finding: 158 Rigvedic mantras carry ONLY a HYMN-level translation (Translation.alignment_level='HYMN'), not a per-mantra one. The committed figure 'RV translation 10,502' and the Work node's '10,502 of 10,552 carry a translation (99.5%)' are both literally true, but per-mantra Rigvedic translation coverage is 10,344/10,552 = 98.03%.

structural_defects.finding: Identical Sanskrit recurs within a single recension: by content_sha256 within one text_role, 190 RV mantras (PRIMARY_TEXT), 349 SV (PRIMARY_TEXT), 6 YV (EXTRACTED_FROM_CONTAINER) and 42 AV (PRIMARY_TEXT) share their text with at least one other mantra of the same recension. In the AV the SEARCH_DERIVATIVE layer collapses far more (256) than the PRIMARY_TEXT does (42), a direct consequence of CORPUS_D01.

where_audio_lives.resolution_semantics: AudioCatalog.resolve walks UP the colon-delimited key and returns levels_above, so a container's recording is reported as a container's recording rather than copied onto each mantra. All 16,834 present records are scope_type MANTRA at levels_above 0.
where_audio_lives.assessed_vs_positive: This is the one optional dimension where 'assessed' IS knowable, because the catalog is an explicit enumerated file rather than an edge that either exists or does not. assessed_vs_never_assessed.headline: For every inherently optional dimension held INSIDE the graph, the graph cannot distinguish 'assessed and came back empty' from 'never assessed'. This is a property of where provenance is written, not a gap in this audit.
assessed_vs_never_assessed.why: Run provenance -- run_id, pipeline_version, method, execution_version, prompt_version, model, score, trust, state -- is written onto the PRODUCED artifact: the dimension relationship itself, or the SemanticAssertion / Formula / FormulaFamily node. It is never written onto the :Mantra that was examined. A :Mantra carries exactly fifteen properties and not one records an enrichment run. There is no assessed-set node, and the 1,072 DerivedMetric nodes hold aggregate distributions by Work, devata and action -- none records an examined population for a dimension.
assessed_vs_never_assessed.consequence: A mantra with no MENTIONS_ENTITY edge is indistinguishable from a mantra the entity detector never read. The absence cannot be typed in the row, only inferred from the pattern of absence across a Veda.
assessed_vs_never_assessed.what_can_still_be_inferred: Because the surviving edges carry run_id, the set of Vedas a run touched is recoverable even though the set of mantras it examined is not. That gives a population-level, not per-passage, answer.

accent_storage.question: Is accent a property, a separate TextVersion, or inline in the Sanskrit string?
accent_storage.answer: All three claims are partly true and only the third is load-bearing. Accent is stored INLINE in TextVersion.text_nfc. TextVersion.accented is a declared boolean that describes the layer, and accent is ALSO the axis on which a recension's several TextVersion layers differ -- so the accented and unaccented readings of the Atharvaveda are two separate TextVersion nodes on the same mantra.

notation_is_not_uniform.RV PRIMARY_TEXT (GRETIL): U+0331 anudatta (101,175 marks) and U+030D svarita (74,801), udatta unmarked.
notation_is_not_uniform.RV PARALLEL_TEXT (VEDAWEB): U+0301 udatta on a vowel (128,482) and U+0300 (2,080). A different convention for the same verses.
notation_is_not_uniform.YV EXTRACTED_FROM_CONTAINER (WIKISOURCE_: Devanagari U+0952 anudatta (24,329) and U+0951 udatta (17,204), plus a single U+1CD4.

accent_storage.flag_vs_string: The accented flag and the measured string agree on 44,275 of 44,276 TextVersion nodes. The single exception is CORPUS_D09.
accent_storage.trap: U+0301 is both the udatta and the palatal sibilant of IAST: s + U+0301 is the letter s-acute, not an accented s. Counting U+0301 by codepoint reports all 5,839 of the AV's deliberately unaccented PARALLEL_TEXT versions as accented (6,789 stray marks). The accent test must require a vowel base. Symmetrically, a codepoint-range test over the Vedic Extensions block counts U+1CEA and U+1CEC -- anusvara signs -- as tone and invents 780 accented Yajurvedic verses in the layer the registry correctly calls unaccented.
